title: Real Assets: from a Formosa General Store to the Waterfront of Buenos Aires
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Las Lomitas, Formosa: the grandfather's counter
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The 1917 emigration and the Formosa general store come from family-history profiles relayed by the Spanish Wikipedia article; the grandfather's given name, Isaac, appears in later family profiles and not in any civil record reached. Sources disagree on the country of departure, Russian Empire or Poland, which for that territory in 1917 is the same disagreement twice. Coordinate is the town of Las Lomitas, not a located building. Date defaulted to 1 January.
stops.campa: A general store on the dust of the Formosa chaco, kept by Isaac Elsztain, who left territory that was Russian Empire when he went and Poland afterward, and reached Argentina in 1917. He sells to cattlemen and to the men who cut quebracho. Whatever real-estate money the family had thins out in the provincial economy, and the accounts are kept in a currency that will not hold still, so he counts what cannot be printed: a square metre, a hectare, a parking space. His grandson will still be quoting the rule to Bloomberg in 2023. The counter, the ledger and the debts owed by men who come to town twice a year are the whole of the business.
stops.quote: People would ask my grandfather, how do you know you're doing well with out of control inflation? He'd say: I want to know if I have one square metre, one more hectare of farm or one more parking space.
stops.quote_source: Eduardo Elsztain to Bloomberg, republished as 'Ex-Soros partner surfs Argentine crisis with real estate empire', Buenos Aires Times, 2023
suggested_refs: Immigration and naturalization records for Elsztain arrivals, Argentina 1917, not reached in this research pass
sources: Bloomberg / Buenos Aires Times, 'Ex-Soros partner surfs Argentine crisis with real estate empire', 2023

stops.name: Belgrano, the family comes down from the provinces
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The Spanish Wikipedia article gives 1950 for the permanent settlement in Buenos Aires; no source reached names an address, and Belgrano as the family's neighbourhood comes from profile material rather than from a civil or press record. Coordinate is the Belgrano pin used across the corpus. Date defaulted to 1 January.
stops.campa: Around 1950 the Elsztains leave the provinces for Buenos Aires and settle in Belgrano, plane trees and low brick on the north side of the city. Mario Julio Elsztain becomes a physician; Alba Rubin teaches. The Jewish immigration that filled the agricultural colonies of Entre Rios and the northern outposts is by this point a city population with its second generation in the professions. No address appears in any record reached, and Belgrano itself comes from profile material rather than from a document. The family stays there for decades.
suggested_refs: Buenos Aires municipal property records for Belgrano, mid-century, not reached in this research pass

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the birth of Eduardo Sergio
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by the English Wikipedia article, citing a Bloomberg Businessweek profile. The parents' names and occupations are attested by the same article. No hospital or sanatorio is named in any source reached, so the coordinate is the corpus Buenos Aires city pin and not a birthplace.
stops.campa: Eduardo Sergio Elsztain is born in Buenos Aires on the twenty-sixth of January 1960, son of a doctor and a teacher, into a house that is comfortable and not rich. Argentina at that moment is six years from its next coup and sixteen from the one after that; the currency he is born under will be renamed and redenominated four times before he is thirty. He is the third generation in the country and the first with no memory of anywhere else. No sanatorio is named in any published account of the day.
suggested_refs: Argentine civil registry birth record, Buenos Aires, 26 January 1960, not reached in this research pass

stops.name: Colegio Nacional de Buenos Aires, Bolivar 263: the class of 1978
stops.date_confidence: Attested. Graduation in 1978 is given by the English Wikipedia article citing the school's own alumni directory at cnba.uba.ar. The directory itself was not opened in this pass. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 1 January. Coordinate is the school building on Bolivar street.
stops.campa: He goes through the Colegio Nacional de Buenos Aires, the state secondary school on Bolivar street that admits by examination and has schooled presidents, and graduates in 1978. The building is a stone pile finished in the 1910s over the ground of the old Jesuit college, and the entrance examination is the hardest in the country. He is there through the years of the junta, when students of this school are among the disappeared. The alumni directory records his year and nothing else.

stops.campa: He enrols at the Universidad de Buenos Aires to read economics, in the building on Avenida Cordoba that faces Plaza Houssay. Some profiles put an earlier attempt at medicine, his father's trade. The state university is free and enormous and, in these years, watched: students of his generation are being taken out of classrooms. He finishes neither degree. Every profile written of him afterward notes the missing one in a single clause, and not one of them explains it.

stops.name: Aguero 1164: the Tanya class and the four thousand dollars
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction throughout, and the whole of it is Chabad institutional memory. The Kabbalah class under Rabbi Avraham Yosef Polichenco, the later Tanya study with Rabbi Tzvi Grunblatt, and Mario Elsztain's four thousand dollar gift under financial strain are told by the movement about itself; no primary Chabad text confirming the figure or the year was located in this pass. Coordinate corrected in verification to Jabad Lubavitch Argentina's own published address, Aguero 1164, approximately -34.599, -58.413; the research pool's -34.5975, -58.4241 sat about 1.2 km west in Almagro. Date defaulted to 1 January.
stops.campa: At the Jabad Lubavitch house on Aguero, in the Abasto, his parents attend a class in Kabbalah given by Rabbi Avraham Yosef Polichenco and afterward study Tanya with Rabbi Tzvi Grunblatt. The family is under financial strain. Mario Elsztain gives the movement four thousand dollars, a sum the movement has not forgotten and retells to itself as the hinge on which everything after it turned. The son is twenty, and the rabbis of Aguero will be in his life for the next forty-five years. No primary Chabad text giving the figure or the year has been found; the account is the movement's memory of itself.

stops.campa: He goes to Jerusalem for volunteer work and courses in leadership, in the way a great many Argentine Jewish twenty-year-olds of that decade went. Nothing about the trip is documented beyond the fact of it: no institution named, no length of stay, no companions. He comes back to a country whose military government is three years from the Malvinas and whose currency is collapsing, and he does not return to medicine and does not return to the faculty on Cordoba. stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. stops.campa: Twenty-four years old and working land deals, he helps broker the sale of two blocks of Belgrano ground to the Soviet Union for its embassy. Argentina and Moscow are grain partners and ideological strangers; the junta has been gone one year and the new democracy is negotiating with everybody. No deed, registry entry or press report of the sale has been found. The transaction is remembered inside Chabad, which tells it about one of its own, and nowhere a researcher can open. The business of it takes him to Moscow.

stops.name: Moscow, matzah in the luggage
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction, and movement tradition specifically. The shmurah matzah carried to Soviet Jews on the embassy-related trip is told by Chabad about one of its own; no independent press or archival source corroborates it, and none was located in this pass. stops.campa: He carries shmurah matzah into the Soviet Union in his luggage, the hand-watched flat bread of Passover, for Jews who can neither bake nor buy it. Possession is not quite a crime and not quite legal. Chabad's couriers to the refuseniks in these years are mostly students and tourists; this one is an Argentine broker travelling on embassy business. The story reaches print only through the movement's own retelling, decades on, when the courier has become its honorary president in Argentina.

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the man who taught him the business
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction as to date and circumstance. Gruber's link to the dormant IRSA vehicle is asserted in the same chain. Coordinate is the corpus Buenos Aires city pin; no meeting place is named anywhere. Date defaulted to 1 January.
stops.campa: Peter Gruber, a fund manager out of the Templeton world and a director of a small listed vehicle called IRSA, comes into his life and stays there as the first teacher. What Gruber has that Buenos Aires does not is access to New York money, and a habit of describing Argentina as an asset class rather than a homeland. The shell company he sits on is dormant and worth almost nothing. El Cronista will run the lesson years later under a headline with no ornament on it: who taught Eduardo Elsztain everything about business.

He is introduced to George Soros, at that moment the most famous currency speculator alive and two years from breaking the Bank of England. Soros gives him roughly ten million dollars to manage. stops.name: 770 Eastern Parkway: move the money
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction as to the specific exchange. stops.campa: On the twelfth of March 1991 he stands in the line at the Rebbe's door in Crown Heights, where Menachem Mendel Schneerson hands out dollar bills and answers in a sentence. He says he is uneasy about a position in the stock market. Schneerson tells him to move the money, without loss, into something safer. A camera is running, as a camera is always running here. Chabad afterward tells the moment as the origin of a fortune. The Convertibility Plan is two weeks old and Soros's ten million is already in his hands.

stops.name: Buenos Aires, a listed company for a hundred and twenty thousand dollars
stops.date_confidence: The June 1991 acquisition of control of IRSA for approximately US$120,000, with Marcelo Mindlin among the partners, is attested by the English Wikipedia article. The marriage to Mariana Carmona in 1991 is attested by the same article citing La Nacion, with no month given. The briefcase of one-dollar notes is reconstruction: it comes from Elsztain's own retelling in a 2024 interview and is not independently documented, and it is marked as his own account rather than as fact. Coordinate is the Buenos Aires stock exchange, chosen as the venue of a listed shell's trading; no meeting place is recorded anywhere.
stops.campa: In June 1991 he and Marcelo Mindlin buy control of Inversiones y Representaciones Sociedad Anonima for about a hundred and twenty thousand dollars. IRSA is a listed company with a name, a history, and almost nothing else. He tells the story afterward with a briefcase of borrowed one-dollar notes in it, carried in to dramatize how small the price was; the briefcase is his own retelling, from 2024, and nothing else confirms it. He is thirty-one, and the listing has cost him less than an apartment. That year he marries Mariana Carmona, a psychologist. La Nacion gives the year and no month.
suggested_refs: Comision Nacional de Valores filings for the 1991 change of control at IRSA, not reached in this research pass

stops.name: Cresud, the farm company taken over
stops.date_confidence: Attested by Cresud's own institutional history at cresud.com.ar, which dates the arrival of Eduardo S. Elsztain as president and Alejandro G. Elsztain as chief executive to 1994, and lists the first Argentine farm purchases immediately after. This corrects the research pool's 1992 entry, which duplicated the same event two years early; there is no 1992 event here. Cresud's foundation in 1936 is from the same history. Coordinate is an approximate microcentro point for the company's Buenos Aires office and is not a verified address. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 1 January.
stops.campa: The group takes Cresud, a farming company listed since 1936 and run down to pasture and debt. Eduardo Elsztain becomes president and his brother Alejandro becomes chief executive. The plan is not to farm. It is to buy Argentine land at the bottom of a long collapse in its price, raise what it yields, and sell it at the top, treating a hectare of Santiago del Estero as an undervalued security. Within two years the company has bought Los Pozos, El Recreo, Tali Sumaj, Runciman, El Silencio and El Gualicho.
suggested_refs: Cresud S.A.C.I.F. y A. institutional history, cresud.com.ar/historia_inst.php

stops.name: New York Stock Exchange, the hundred and ten million
stops.date_confidence: Attested by the English Wikipedia article: IRSA enters international markets via the NYSE in December 1994, raising US$110 million. Cresud's own US listing is separate and later, NASDAQ in 1997-98 with a US$92 million capital increase, per the company's institutional history. Day unknown, defaulted to 1.
stops.campa: In December 1994 IRSA lists in New York and raises a hundred and ten million dollars, after months of roadshows through the United States and Europe explaining Argentine real estate to fund managers who have mostly heard of the country in connection with default. Three weeks later Mexico devalues and the Tequila crisis takes Buenos Aires down with it. The money is already raised, and it is in dollars. It will be spent, over the next four years, buying from people who have to sell.

stops.name: Los Pozos, Salta: the chaco bought by the hectare
stops.date_confidence: Attested that Cresud bought Los Pozos in the 1995-96 purchase round, per the company's own institutional history. This corrects the research pool, which carried 1973 as the development date and tagged the whole stop attested: whatever 1973 refers to, it is not a Cresud or Elsztain date, since the takeover was 1994. The Greenpeace clearing figures are reconstruction and belong to the 2019 stop, not here. Coordinate is an approximate point in the Salta chaco land-development zone, not a surveyed boundary. Month and day defaulted.
stops.campa: Cresud buys Los Pozos in the Salta chaco, one of six properties taken across the north in two years and named as such in the company's own history of itself. It becomes the largest holding in the portfolio and eventually the most contested. The model requires the clearing: buy undeveloped, develop, revalue, hold or sell. Provincial permits are issued and the dry forest comes down for pasture and then for soy, at a rate satellites will measure twenty years later. The quebracho and the palo santo go first.
stops.quote: My theory for the last 20 years, since we've lived through crisis and the depths Argentina sank to in 2002, is that our defense against liquidity is real assets.
stops.quote_source: Eduardo Elsztain to Bloomberg, republished in the Buenos Aires Times, 2023, said long after this purchase and describing its logic

stops.name: Alto Palermo, the shopping centres
stops.date_confidence: Attested by the Spanish Wikipedia article on IRSA: Alto Palermo acquired 1996, Patio Bullrich acquired across 1996-1998. Coordinate for Patio Bullrich, mentioned here but not given its own stop, was corrected in verification to -34.5886, -58.3838 at Avenida del Libertador 750; the research pool's value sat several blocks west. stops.campa: IRSA buys the Alto Palermo shopping centre on Santa Fe, and over the following two years Patio Bullrich in Recoleta, the auction house of the cattle aristocracy already converted into a mall in the eighties. The convertibility peso is worth a dollar and Argentines are shopping. The group's method is now legible: acquire the built landmark rather than build it, hold the ground under it, and let the rent service the debt that bought the next one. Two more will follow before the decade closes.

stops.name: The old Ciudad Deportiva de Boca: the empty ground on the river
stops.date_confidence: The 1997 acquisition of the former Boca Juniors sports-city land is attested by the English Wikipedia article. The area is a live contradiction, flagged and not resolved: the same English article gives 22 hectares, while IRSA's own Ramblas del Plata material and a later SEC filing give about 70 hectares. Coordinate needs a fresh fix and is given here as an approximation: the research pool's -34.61, -58.355 falls inside the Reserva Ecologica Costanera Sur, and the reclaimed sports-city land lies south of the reserve, nearer -34.628, -58.353. The Spanish articles for Ciudad Deportiva and Solares de Santa Maria returned 404 and ramblasdelplata.com returned no text. Month and day defaulted.
stops.campa: IRSA buys the abandoned sports city of Boca Juniors, land pushed out into the Rio de la Plata in the sixties for a stadium that was never finished. The club needs money and the parcel is enormous and useless. It will sit empty through two currency regimes, one default, a rezoning fight and a reversed court injunction, for twenty-seven years. How enormous it is has never been settled: the English record says twenty-two hectares, the company's own later material says about seventy, and nothing reached reconciles them. Which figure describes the ground he bought?

Citicorp is selling down its Argentine holdings and IRSA is buying; the hotel is a third kind of building for a group that already owns malls and farms. It is an unremarkable purchase in a year of purchases, and nothing in the record suggests anyone thinks about it again for twenty-five years.

stops.campa: On the ninth of November 1998 the Mercado de Abasto reopens as a shopping centre. IRSA bought it in 1996, shut and rotting since 1984, and spent two years restoring the raw concrete naves that Viktor Sulcic and his partners raised over Corrientes in the thirties: no plaster, no cladding, the structure standing as the elevation. The president and the mayor come to the opening. The neighbourhood keeps the market's name and its facade, and loses the market itself.

stops.campa: The national mortgage bank is privatized, the law in 1997 and the share offering in 1999, and the IRSA group takes a stake that grows into effective private control, with Elsztain chairman from 2009. Criminal complaints over the privatization name him alongside the economy minister Roque Fernandez, Daniel Marx and the bank director Pablo Rojo, alleging illicit association, fraud against the public administration, usury and abuse of authority. No conviction follows. The cases record no significant judicial progress against him.
stops.quote: La sociedad argentina tiene mucho ahorro y muy poco crédito. Y está traumada.

The country is weeks into the farm strike over export duties, the roads out of the pampa are blocked, and the president is receiving one of the largest private owners of Argentine farmland. Argentina acquires, without anybody having decided to create it, a room where the owners of the country talk to whoever is going to govern it.
